Fun until you hit the end game and the infinite grind, then it's just about letting the game play by itself in the background while you do something else. Putting together a team and customizing them through your equipment to overcome the various challenges you encounter throughout the game (up to level 1000 or so) is the best part. Game has unlocks upwards of level 2,000,000 though, and the fastest you'll be moving through floors is about 5,000 floors per hour, so it'll take a LOT of AFKing.

In my view, the most enjoyable aspect of the game is enhancing your party's efficiency to advance through the maximum number of floors to collect gold, mythics, and essence. I also found the challenge of optimizing boss rushes to be engaging.
The option to customize specific actions for each party member offers a level of personalization that is seldom found in idle games.

All in all a good sequel with notable improvements, but still grindy and repetitive. It's an idle game so you know it's part of the package. Many paid ones pale in comparison to Soda Dungeon however.

Soda Dungeon 2 is one of the best sequels to a game I've ever seen. It expands upon what made SD1 so fun, and it also introduces new mechanics that lead to more complex and interesting strategies. For example, you can now create custom scripts for your team, telling them exactly how you want them to fight. While it's confusing to figure out at first, the power of scripts in this game should not be underestimated, and it's absolutely worth figuring them out and how you want to play SD2. SD2 also has a more developed late-game than SD1, as there's more gear and upgrades that you can unlock even after hundreds of hours. It's clear that Armor Games put a lot of love into this sequel, and if you like to play idle games, then you should definitely give this game a try.

Game Enjoyability: 8/10

I 100%ed SD1 years ago and it is honestly the best idle game I've ever tried. SD2 is basically an improved version of the first game. It has the same essence but with way more strategy.

They added some GREAT stuff like offline progress and custom AI scripts to have better control of how your team fights in auto-mode. Also, mechanics like crafting seem useless until you realize how important they are for challenges like Boss Rush. You can't just rely on relics and being super OP anymore, so you have to play smart.

Play SD1 if you want a purely simple idle experience in the background while working or studying. If you want an idle game where you actually have to think (just a little bit) about your strategy and how the game works, SD2 is the way to go.

As much as I won't recommend the mobile version as the "true version" (because of ads mainly, but who can blame the devs honestly), this game is still very amazing. 
I insisted on finishing the 100% before my review, but even then i didn't feel as much as what can people consider idler games. Even though the second to second loop is repetitive, there is still so much optimization, upgrades, items to unlock, objectives to go to. So, even if you get bored and get back to it eventually, you can still find stuff to do in the background.

I have a lot of playtime in Soda Dungeon 1 (SD1), before moving to SD2.

I'm a skeptical guy so I seriously thought that SD2 would just be "the same game, but now with microtransactions and some additional cheap ideas". Turns out it isn't the case here. It's a clear step up from its SD1, there's a story now with humor and creative aspects, more ways in how you gain money / power / ability to move up the ladder. I gotta emphasize on the humor that it has and there's so many little funny things that just make me chuckle.

It's a free game, with nice content and ideas, it fits guys like me who just doesn't bother spending medium+ efforts on video games. Of course microtransactions are there and eventually you'll have to spend a lot of time having this game open just to have a run happen, but the sole idea of wanting to have the game opened just says it for me.

The game is [b]really cool, even though I preferred its [u]predecessor[/u]![/b]
I don’t plan on continuing to play after getting all the achievements, because I no longer feel like spending thousands of hours grinding the same game (hi, Summoners War, WoW, and Lost Ark), but I understand those who do. 
[b]I definitely recommend playing it...[/b] at least up to the [b]Warrior Dimension![/b] (the start of the “infinite” grind)
One of the best free-to-play casual RPGs for me. Its pixelised graphics give it a great retro vibe, and the whole soda-themed concept is unique. I definitely recommend it.

Holy time sink. SD2 is a fun little game to have running in the background, but after you get into the late midgame or early endgame the runs take forever and most of your play time will be afk. I'd only recommend it if you like wasting time or having multiple games running to scratch that incremental game itch.

Not much has changed since the game released. The custom scripts are in a much better place now but can still be a little finnicky at times. There have been buffs to the different synergies and play styles but there is still a fairly defined meta.

There are quite a few guides out there to help steer you in the right direction for dimension 1-10 but there isn't a cohesive wiki for things like drop rates and niche mechanics. The fandom wiki exists but doesn't help much in the grand scheme of things.

Overall 7/10. Mindless background progression can be fun at times.

Even other "endless" idlers keep some very high level progression carrot that is worth your time/interest.

reviews.title: Soda Dungeon 2 is LEGENDARY.
reviews.text: This game in it’s 1st release as Soda Dungeon 1/(OG) helped me through horrible times in high school. playing this sequel 5 years later has helped so much. Plus the improvements are absolutely immaculate and amazing. Please keep up the good work on this and I hope to see a part three if possible in the future because I will play every single released edition of this until the day I die. This has actually been one of my favorite gaming series and it has been extremely hard to find one that I truly enjoy besides Legend of Zelda. thank you guys.

reviews.title: I love this game
reviews.text: I love traveling through dimensions, fighting quirky bosses and strategizing what characters use what etc. I also really like how you can customize the auto battle you can adjust it to your playsyle or even make specialized scripts for each character. I honestly can’t see why it’s a more popular game.

reviews.title: Why?
reviews.text: When selling equipment, when I have both basic and leveled-up versions of some particular piece of equipment, why does it combine them into one entry in the list of equipment?  And it doesn’t tell me the total count, but rather the number of *leveled-up* ones first.  To sell the basic versions, I have to sell *all the leveled-up versions first*.  Why?  That’s madness.

reviews.title: To many ads
reviews.text: Was great, now there’s to many ads. Ruins the immersiveness, and how fluid it used to feel. I don’t like forced ads, and they shouldn’t happen after every dungeon run. Can’t believe I have to play offline to avoid this.
